title: CSRF trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for csrf trace events.

defences.description: What the site has switched on against forged requests.

sameSite.description: The SameSite attribute of the session cookie; untranslated.

csrfToken.description: Whether the server requires a synchronizer token on state-changing requests.

originCheck.description: Whether the server compares the Origin header with its own origin.

postOnly.description: Whether state changes are refused on safe methods (GET, HEAD).

auth.description: Where the session lives: an ambient cookie, or a header the app attaches.

corsReflectsOrigin.description: Whether the API echoes any Origin back with credentials allowed.

session.description: The credential the attack tries to borrow.

ambient.description: Whether the browser attaches it by itself, without the page asking.

token.description: The synchronizer token bound to the session, or null when none is used.

request.description: The request being traced (null before the first one).

origin.description: The origin of the page that built the request.

delivery.description: How the request was produced; untranslated.

markup.description: The snippet on the page that causes the request.

crossSite.description: Whether the page that built it belongs to another site.

userInitiated.description: Whether the user actually asked for this action.

credentials.description: Whether the session travelled with the request.

token.description: The CSRF token the request carries, or null when it carries none.

reached.description: Whether the request left the browser and reached the server.

outcome.description: How far the current request got and what the server decided.

stage.description: Progress: nothing yet, page built it, server received it, verdict final.

authenticated.description: Whether the server accepted the session behind the request.

performed.description: Whether the state change actually happened.

blockedBy.description: Which layer stopped it; null when nothing did.

responseReadable.description: Whether the page that built the request may read the response.

account.description: What the forged requests actually cost.

stolen.description: How much has ended up in the attacker's account.

stats.description: Running totals across the whole run.

forged.description: State changes the user never asked for.

blocked.description: Requests stopped by the browser or refused by the server.
